events.title: Sysmon Event 1 — Process creation

overview.summary: Records creation of a new process with execution context including full command line, stable ProcessGuid correlation, configured image hashes, logon/session context and parent-process details.
security_value: reconstruct process creation and parent/child execution chains
correlate process activity across Sysmon events with ProcessGuid
investigate suspicious command lines, executable paths and integrity context
pivot from process execution to network, DNS, image-load and process-access telemetry

requirements: Sysmon must be installed and running.
The active Sysmon EventFiltering configuration must not exclude the ProcessCreate activity required by the investigation.
collection.configuration_note: ProcessCreate is a filterable Sysmon event. Collection volume and exclusions should be governed for the environment without removing required security visibility.
collection.hash_note: Image hashes reflect the hash algorithms configured for Sysmon and may contain multiple algorithm/value pairs.

correlations.purpose: network activity attributed to the created process
process termination and lifetime
image/module load context when ImageLoad is enabled
process-access context
DNS query context
parent/child process-chain reconstruction
Windows process-creation corroboration
correlations.limitation: Windows can reuse PIDs; ProcessGuid is preferred within Sysmon and time/context are required for cross-provider correlation

analysis: Review unusual parent/child chains, script interpreters, LOLBins and execution from user-writable or temporary paths.
Inspect full command lines, image metadata, configured hashes, user/logon context and integrity level together rather than treating any single field as a malicious verdict.
Use ParentProcessGuid and ProcessGuid to reconstruct execution lineage, then pivot to network, DNS, image-load and process-access telemetry where available.
Treat file-version metadata such as Company, Product, Description and OriginalFileName as contextual claims from the executable metadata, not proof of trust.

fields.meaning: Rule metadata associated with the Sysmon filter rule that produced the event when present.
UTC timestamp recorded for the process creation event.
Sysmon-generated process GUID intended to provide stable correlation for the process even when Windows reuses process IDs.
fields.correlation: Preferred process correlation key across Sysmon events.

fields.meaning: Windows process identifier assigned to the newly created process.
fields.correlation: Use with ProcessGuid and time because PID values can be reused.

fields.meaning: Executable image path for the newly created process.
File-version metadata reported for the executable image when available.
File-description metadata reported by the executable image when available.
Product-name metadata reported by the executable image when available.
Company/publisher metadata reported by the executable image when available; this value is contextual and is not a trust decision.
Original-file-name metadata embedded in the executable image when available; it may differ from the current path or filename.
Full command line recorded for the newly created process.
Working directory associated with the newly created process.
User/security-principal context associated with the newly created process.
Sysmon session/logon GUID associated with the process when available.
fields.correlation: Use to pivot among events associated with the same logon/session context where populated consistently.

fields.meaning: Windows logon-session identifier associated with the process.
fields.correlation: May be correlated with Windows logon/security telemetry when provider semantics and timing align.

fields.meaning: Terminal Services session identifier associated with the process.
Integrity level reported for the process security context.
Configured hash values for the process image, potentially containing multiple algorithm/value pairs.
fields.notes: Available algorithms depend on the active Sysmon hash configuration.

fields.meaning: Sysmon-generated GUID of the parent process.
fields.correlation: Primary Sysmon key for parent/child process-chain reconstruction.

fields.meaning: Windows process identifier of the parent process.
fields.correlation: Use with ParentProcessGuid and time because PID values can be reused.

fields.meaning: Executable image path recorded for the parent process.
Command line recorded for the parent process.
User/security-principal context recorded for the parent process.

events.title: Sysmon Event 2 — A process changed a file creation time
aliases: A process changed a file creation time
events.source_locator: Events > Event ID 2: A process changed a file creation time

overview.summary: Records a process changing a file creation timestamp and preserves both the new and previous UTC creation times with process identity for investigation.
security_value: identify file creation-time changes that may indicate timestomping or anti-forensic activity
attribute timestamp changes to a stable Sysmon process identity
compare new and previous creation times during file-system timeline reconstruction
correlate timestamp changes with process creation and related file activity

requirements: Sysmon must be installed and running.
The active Sysmon EventFiltering configuration must not exclude the FileCreateTime activity required by the investigation.
collection.interpretation_note: Legitimate applications can modify file creation times. Collection and analysis should preserve process and surrounding file activity so timestamp changes are not treated as a malicious verdict by themselves.

correlations.purpose: process creation and execution context for the process changing the timestamp
related file creation or overwrite activity
related file deletion activity where those event classes are collected
Windows process-creation corroboration
correlations.limitation: PID values can be reused; ProcessGuid is preferred inside Sysmon

analysis: Compare CreationUtcTime with PreviousCreationUtcTime and the surrounding file-system timeline to identify suspicious backdating or other anomalous timestamp changes.
Use ProcessGuid to pivot to the process creation record and related Sysmon activity before deciding whether the timestamp change is suspicious.
Prioritize timestamp changes made by unusual processes, script interpreters, LOLBins or executables from user-writable locations, while accounting for legitimate software behavior.
Treat Event 2 as observation telemetry rather than a malicious verdict.

fields.meaning: Rule metadata associated with the Sysmon filter rule that produced the event when present.
UTC timestamp recorded for the file creation-time change event.
Sysmon-generated process GUID for the process that changed the file creation time.
fields.correlation: Preferred process correlation key across Sysmon events.

fields.meaning: Windows process identifier of the process that changed the file creation time.
fields.correlation: Use with ProcessGuid and time because PID values can be reused.

fields.meaning: Executable image path of the process that changed the file creation time.
Path of the file whose creation timestamp was changed.
fields.correlation: Use with time and related file events to reconstruct file activity.

fields.meaning: Creation timestamp recorded after the file creation-time change.
File creation timestamp recorded before the change, preserved for comparison with the resulting value.
User/security-principal context associated with the process that changed the file creation time.

events.title: Sysmon Event 3 — Network connection detected

overview.summary: Records process-associated TCP and UDP network connection activity with source and destination network context.
security_value: attribute network activity to a process
pivot between process execution and remote infrastructure
investigate unusual destinations, ports and connection patterns
reconstruct process/network timelines

requirements: Sysmon must be installed and running.
NetworkConnect collection must be enabled by configuration because Event ID 3 is disabled by default.
collection.volume_note: Network connection telemetry can be high-volume; use governed include/exclude filtering appropriate to the environment.

correlations.purpose: process creation context
process lifetime/termination
process access context
DNS context
Windows process-creation corroboration
correlations.limitation: PID can be reused; ProcessGuid is preferred inside Sysmon

analysis: Review script interpreters, LOLBins or user-writable executables establishing unexpected external connections.
Prioritize unusual process-to-destination combinations, uncommon ports and repeated periodic connections.
Treat Event 3 as observation telemetry, not a malicious verdict.

fields.meaning: Rule metadata associated with the Sysmon filter rule that produced the event when present.
UTC time recorded for the network connection event.
Sysmon-generated process GUID used as the preferred process correlation identifier.
fields.correlation: Prefer this over PID because Windows can reuse process IDs.

fields.meaning: Windows process identifier associated with the connection.
fields.correlation: Use with Image and time when correlating outside Sysmon; PID alone is not globally unique.

fields.meaning: Executable image path associated with the network connection.
Account context associated with the process.
Transport protocol recorded for the connection, commonly TCP or UDP.
Direction indicator; true denotes a connection initiated by the process in applicable Sysmon telemetry.

Source hostname when name resolution provides a value.
Source port recorded for the connection.
Friendly source service/port name when available.

Remote destination IP address recorded for the connection.

Remote destination port recorded for the connection.
Friendly destination service/port name when available.

events.title: Sysmon Event 4 — Sysmon service state changed
events.source_locator: Events > Event ID 4: Sysmon service state changed

overview.summary: Reports a Sysmon service state transition, including the service state together with the Sysmon binary version and active schema version for telemetry continuity analysis.
security_value: identify Sysmon service starts and stops that affect telemetry availability
detect unexpected service interruption or restart for investigation
record the Sysmon and schema versions associated with a service transition
correlate service-state changes with configuration changes, errors and surrounding host activity

requirements: Sysmon must be installed on the host.
The Sysmon Operational channel must be collected and retained for the investigation window.
collection.configuration_note: Event 4 is a Sysmon service state event and is not filterable through an EventFiltering tag.
collection.interpretation_note: A service stop or start can be legitimate during maintenance, upgrade or reboot. Treat the event as telemetry availability evidence rather than a malicious verdict.

correlations.purpose: determine whether a service transition occurred near a Sysmon configuration change
identify nearby Sysmon internal errors that may explain telemetry disruption
review process execution around unexpected service-state transitions

analysis: Establish whether the reported state change aligns with an approved reboot, upgrade, maintenance window or administrative action.
Investigate unexpected stops or repeated restart patterns because they can reduce host telemetry visibility, while avoiding treating the event alone as proof of tampering.
Record Version and SchemaVersion when comparing telemetry behavior across hosts or before and after upgrades.
Correlate the transition time with Sysmon configuration changes, internal errors and relevant process-execution telemetry to determine operational or security context.

fields.meaning: UTC timestamp recorded for the Sysmon service state transition.
Reported Sysmon service state for the transition, such as a started or stopped state.
Sysmon runtime version reported with the service state transition.
Sysmon configuration schema version reported with the service state transition.

events.title: Sysmon Event 5 — Process terminated

overview.summary: Records termination of a process and preserves stable process identity and execution context so analysts can complete process timelines and correlate related Sysmon activity.
security_value: complete process execution timelines by pairing process termination with process creation
identify short-lived or unexpectedly terminating processes when surrounding context warrants investigation
correlate the terminated process with other Sysmon telemetry through ProcessGuid
support duration and lifecycle analysis without treating normal process exit as a malicious verdict

requirements: Sysmon must be installed and running.
The active Sysmon EventFiltering configuration must not exclude the ProcessTerminate activity required by the investigation.
collection.configuration_note: ProcessTerminate is a filterable Sysmon event. Exclusions should be governed so required lifecycle visibility is preserved.
collection.interpretation_note: Process termination is routine operating-system activity. Event 5 provides lifecycle evidence and should be interpreted with process creation and surrounding telemetry rather than as a malicious verdict by itself.

correlations.purpose: pair process creation and termination to reconstruct process lifetime
review network activity associated with the process before termination
review DNS activity associated with the process before termination

analysis: Pair Event 5 with Sysmon Event 1 using ProcessGuid to reconstruct process lifetime and surrounding execution context.
Review unusually short-lived or repeatedly terminating processes only in conjunction with image path, user context, process creation data and related telemetry.
Use ProcessGuid as the preferred Sysmon correlation key because Windows process IDs can be reused over time.
Treat Event 5 as process-lifecycle observation telemetry rather than evidence of maliciousness by itself.

fields.meaning: Rule metadata associated with the Sysmon filter rule that produced the process termination event when present.
UTC timestamp recorded for the process termination event.
Sysmon-generated process GUID identifying the terminated process.
fields.correlation: Preferred process correlation key across Sysmon lifecycle and activity events.

fields.meaning: Windows process identifier of the terminated process.
fields.correlation: Use with ProcessGuid and time because PID values can be reused.

fields.meaning: Executable image path recorded for the terminated process.
User or security-principal context associated with the terminated process.

events.title: Windows Security Event 4624 — An account was successfully logged on
events.source_locator: 4624(S): An account was successfully logged on

overview.summary: Records creation of a successful logon session on the destination computer.

event_versions.notes: Adds Logon Information fields including Restricted Admin Mode, Virtual Account, Elevated Token, Linked Logon ID and network-account fields.

overview.newer_provider_note: Controlled Windows Server 2025 provider evidence contains the current Event 4624 identity; newer fields such as Remote Credential Guard are represented only where structural/provider evidence and reviewed semantics permit.

requirements: Audit Logon success auditing must be enabled for the applicable audit policy/subcategory.
collection.privacy_note: Identity and network-origin fields can contain security-sensitive operational context; access to exported event data should follow organizational policy.

correlations.purpose: session logoff
user-initiated logoff
special privileges assigned to the session
process activity associated with the logon session
Kerberos service-ticket context
correlations.limitation: Correlation depends on populated/consistent GUID values and authentication path

correlations.purpose: origin validation

analysis: Investigate unexpected RemoteInteractive (type 10) sessions, unusual network logons, privileged identities from new origins and service accounts using interactive logon types.
Correlate successful logons with preceding 4625 failures and subsequent 4672/4688 activity when investigating authentication sequences.
Treat 4624 as successful-session telemetry, not a malicious verdict.

logon_type.meaning: Network logon in which cleartext-capable credentials are supplied to the authentication package; this does not mean the password necessarily traverses the network as plaintext.

logon_type.name: NewCredentials
logon_type.meaning: Local identity is retained while alternate credentials are used for outbound network connections.

logon_type.name: RemoteInteractive
logon_type.meaning: Remote interactive logon such as Remote Desktop/Terminal Services.

logon_type.name: CachedInteractive
logon_type.meaning: Interactive logon using cached domain credentials.

events.title: Windows Security Event 4688 — A new process has been created
aliases: A new process has been created
events.source_locator: 4688(S): A new process has been created

overview.summary: Records creation of a new process and identifies the creator security context, target security context where applicable, process identity, parent process context, elevation state and optional command-line data.

event_versions.notes: Adds Process Command Line when the required policy is enabled.
Renames Subject to Creator Subject and adds Target Subject, Mandatory Label and Creator Process Name.

requirements: Audit Process Creation success auditing must be enabled.
To populate Process Command Line, enable the policy that includes command-line data in process creation events.
collection.privacy_note: Process command lines can contain sensitive arguments. Collection, retention and access should follow organizational policy.

correlations.key: Creator Subject Logon ID / Target Subject Logon ID
correlations.purpose: associate process creation with the relevant logon session
identify termination of the created process

correlations.key: Creator Process ID ↔ earlier New Process ID
correlations.purpose: reconstruct parent/child process lineage

correlations.key: PID + image + time, preferring Sysmon ProcessGuid inside Sysmon
correlations.purpose: enrich process creation with Sysmon context
identify sessions that received special privileges

analysis: Review unusual parent/child process chains, execution from user-writable paths, suspicious command lines and unexpected elevated-token use.
Correlate Logon ID with identity/session events and New Process ID with later process/network/file activity.
Treat Event 4688 as execution telemetry; suspiciousness depends on process, user, parent, command line, integrity and surrounding activity.

token_elevation_type.name: Type 3 — Limited token
token_elevation_type.meaning: UAC-filtered standard token with administrative privileges/groups removed or disabled.
